summary:
Agriculture in dry regions like Oman faces major challenges due to water shortages and the loss of rainwater through seasonal flash floods in wadis. Traditional irrigation methods often follow fixed schedules instead of actual soil conditions, leading to water waste and affecting crop growth.
​To address these challenges and the NASA Space Apps Challenge theme "Adapting Farms Using NASA Data," we developed SoinFlit, a low-cost smart agricultural water management system that combines NASA's open data with ground-level Internet of Things (IoT) technology.
​The system uses NASA satellite datasets, including GPM IMERG for rainfall, SMAP for soil moisture, MODIS for vegetation health, and SRTM for land elevation. This data helps identify areas that collect water and areas affected by drought. On the ground, we use an ESP32 microcontroller with a soil moisture sensor to collect real-time data and send it to the ThingSpeak cloud platform.
​Our system compares satellite data with ground sensor readings to identify the actual water needs of farms and distribute stored rainwater to areas that need it most. We also developed a web dashboard to display maps, water tank levels, and water distribution suggestions.
​Through SoinFlit, we aim to reduce water waste, protect farms, improve water management, and support sustainable agriculture in Oman. The project also raises public awareness about water conservation and the importance of monitoring soil and vegetation.
details:
Agriculture in arid regions like Oman faces severe water shortages and rainwater loss from seasonal flash floods, while traditional fixed-schedule irrigation wastes water and harms crop growth. To address the "Adapting Farms Using NASA Data" challenge, we developed SoinFlit—a low-cost smart agricultural water management system that combines NASA open satellite data with ground Internet of Things (IoT) sensors.

​SoinFlit integrates NASA datasets—GPM IMERG (rainfall), SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS (vegetation health), and SRTM (elevation)—to identify water-collection zones and drought-affected areas. On the ground, Arduino UNO and ESP32 microcontrollers connected to soil moisture, rainfall, and water-level sensors collect real-time field data and send it to the ThingSpeak cloud platform. This automates a relay-controlled DC water pump and displays live maps, tank levels, and smart water distribution recommendations on the SoinFlit application and web dashboard.

​Built using C and C++ (for sensor and pump programming in Arduino IDE) alongside HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and MATLAB analytics, our solution creatively bridges macro-level space observations with low-cost farm automation. During development, we prioritized affordability, reliability in harsh climates, and a user-friendly interface. Ultimately, SoinFlit reduces water waste, protects farms from flash floods, supports sustainable agriculture in Oman, and raises awareness about smart water conservation.
